Conclusions
The binder of paraf ﬁn based multi-component has been used in the W –Cu tube
extrusion molding, the extrusion molding process is stable, the W –Cu tube product
performance is stable, and the repeatability is good. The sintering temperature and
time are the key factors to affect the microstructure and properties of W –Cu alloy
tube. High properties of W –30%Cu tube with a relative density of 99.6% and an
electric conductivity of 49%IACS are obtained when sintering at 1300 °C for 2 h
and the powder loading is up to 60%.

and Characterizations of Powder
Metallurgy Targets for Integrated

Zhaochong Ding, Xiao Liu, Yonghui Wang, Zhuang Wang,
Qiankun Xia and Yongjun Li
Abstract Many refractory metal and alloy ﬁlms are used in Integrate Circuits
processing for varied applications, such as plug, barrier layer, glue layer, gate layer,
bond-pad, and etc. Usually these ﬁlms are deposited from powder metallurgy
(PM) targets including tungsten, tungsten titanium alloy, molybdenum, silicide
alloy, chromium, ruthenium, and etc. On one hand, sintering fabrication methods
for these targets, such as atmospheric pressure sintering, Hot Pressing (HP), Hot
Isostatic Pressing (HIP) and Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS), are presented in this
paper. And the in ﬂuence of sintering methods on the target ’s performance is also
discussed. On another hand, the characterizations of powder metallurgy targets are
also discussed, such as purity, density, grain size, grain orientation, and uniformity.

## Page 981

Introduction
Lots of refractory metals and alloy are used for varied application in the fabrication
process of integrate circuits (IC) devices. For example, tungsten (W) ﬁlm is used as
diffusion barrier, via, and gate layer [ 1]. Silicide alloy ﬁlm, such as WSix, MoSix,
TaSix, is used as contact layer on polysilicon gate which can withstand the high
temperature processing step in front end processing of IC [ 2]. Titanium tungsten
(TiW) alloy ﬁlm is used as diffusion barrier for advanced packaging.
Ruthenium (Ru), Ruthenium –Tantalum (Ru–Ta) and Ruthenium –Titanium (Ru–
Ti) alloys have the potential to be used as barrier layer at or below 15 nm tech-
nology generation [ 3]. For the under bump metallization (UBM) package process,
an adhesion and barrier layers can be Cr, W, TiW, etc. The wetting layer is Ti or
TiW layer [ 4]. These ﬁlms are commonly formed by sputtering corresponding
targets, which are mostly fabricated by powder metallurgy (PM) sintering method
due to the high melting point. And the sintering methods commonly include
atmospheric pressure sintering, Hot Pressing (HP), Hot Isostatic Pressing (HIP) and
Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) and so on.
In order to achieve the fabrication and application requirement of ﬁlms, purity,
density, grain size, grain orientation are the major performance factors of the PM
target which needs to be strictly controlled [ 5]. Generally speaking, purity may
affect the ﬁlm properties and reliability, while density, grain size and grain orien-
tation may affect the particle generation and ﬁlm uniformity. And it is considered
that the high quality PM target should be high purity, high density, ﬁne and
equal-axed grains, without or weak grain orientation. For the PM target, the per-
formance is closely linked with sintering method. In this paper the features of the
above sintering methods and the in ﬂuence of the target performance would be
compared and discussed. And the characterization of the target, including purity,
density, grain size and grain orientation, was also discussed.
Fabrication of the PM Target
Atmospheric Pressure Sintering Atmospheric pressure sintering is the sintering
of a powder compact without applied pressure in the PM process. Usually the
powder compact can be created by Cold Isostatic Pressing (CIP) into a plastic
capsule, and then the ﬁnal green compact is heated to sinter in a furnace. Since the
targets for IC are generally high purity metals or alloy, so the sinter furnace is
required to be high vacuum, hydrogen gas or inert gas atmosphere which protects
the targets from contamination. The characteristics of atmospheric pressure sin-
tering are that the sintering equipment is low cost, and the targets even with a large
dimension can be manufactured in low cost and in large quantities [ 6]. However,
the disadvantages of pressureless sintering are obvious. Firstly the density of the
pressureless sintering target is usually lower than 95% of the theoretical density.
1012 Z. Ding et al.

## Page 982

In order to reach high density, the target needs to sinter under high sintering
temperature for long time. So the grain size of the target is prone to grow too large
which is not expected. Secondly the technology process is especially strict with the
rate of temperature rising and cooling, otherwise the target is prone to curve and
distort even crack. To solve the problem of low density, the target after atmospheric
pressure sintering is subsequently processed with the thermo-mechanical treatment,
such as HIP and hot rolling [ 7]. Take W, Mo and alloy target for example, one
manufacturing process is that ﬁrstly CIP the powder into a green compact, then
atmospheric pressure sintering the compact in hydrogen atmosphere to a solidi ﬁed
blank, and then the blank proceeded with hot rolling and recrystallization annealing.
After the hot rolling, the target density can greatly increase and almost reach
theoretical density [ 8]. And through the recrystallization annealing, the grains of the
target after hot rolling can also be re ﬁned to some extent. For Fig. 1, just after
atmospheric pressure sintering, the grains of Mo blank are ﬁne and equal-axed and
uniform, and the shape is similar with that of the raw powder. But the density of the
Mo blank is less than 95% with few ﬁne pores in the blank which would affect the
particle generation during sputtering [ 9, 10]. For Fig. 2, after atmospheric pressure
sintering and hot rolling, the grains of Mo blank are stretched to band which is
parallel to the rolling direction, and the density can reach more than 99.5% of the
theoretical density.
HP HP is a PM process of simultaneously applying pressure and sintering on the
loose powder or the green compact. In most of the cases the loose powder or the
green compact is ﬁlled into a graphite or Carbon –Carbon composite, or Al
2O3
mould, which allows heating up to sintering temperature. Through applying hot
pressure up to 20 –50 MPa, which can induce the powder particle rearrangement
and plastic ﬂow at the particle contacts and reduce the sintering temperature, so the
target is prone to fully dense and even reach theoretical density with ﬁne grain size
[11]. During the HP process of high temperature and high vacuum atmosphere or

inert atmosphere, the gas and low melting metals impurities in the powder are easily
decreased by off-gas pump system connected with the HP furnace, which improves
the target purity to some extent. Besides, the target after HP is near net-shape,
which minimizes additional ﬁnished target machining [ 12, 13]. However the pro-
duction efﬁciency of HP is low and the target production is only several pieces for
every batch, because there is density non-uniformity between the targets of the
same batch when the total thickness of targets is too large. And the target dimension
is limited to that of the mould and HP furnace. The bigger of the target dimension,
the easier the mould deforms even cracks. And the bigger of the HP furnace, the
higher of its cost. Figure 3 is the schematic diagram of the HP mould, which is

## Page 984

HIP HIP, the same with HP, is also a process of simultaneously applying pressure
and sintering on the powder or the green compact. But the HIP pressure high up to
100–200 MPa is gas isostatic and the gas media most widely used is inert gas such
as argon, so that the material does not chemically react [ 14]. During the HIP
process, the powder or green compact after CIP is placed in container, typically a
steel, titanium, or molybdenum can depending the powder material. The container
is subjected to elevated temperature and very high vacuum to remove air and
moisture from the powder. The container is then sealed and HIP. The application of
high inert gas and elevated temperatures results in the removal of the internal voids
and make the target density reach near 100%. Comparing to HP with one or two
axel pressure, the HIP is isostatic pressure and the pressure is much higher and the
sintering temperature can be much lower. So the grains in the target are much ﬁner
and more uniform [ 15]. The HIP can also realize batch production which decreases
the single piece cost. But the cost of the HIP equipment and running is much higher
than HP or atmospheric pressure sintering, and the target dimension especially the
diameter is limited to the HIP equipment. Meanwhile the manufacture process of
the HIP container is very complex and the container performance is strictly
requirement. The gas and moisture in the powder must be fully removed to avoid
high gas impurity in the target. The container must be completely high vacuum
sealed during HIP to create internal- external pressure difference.
SPS SPS is a newly developing rapid sintering process based on the electrical
spark discharge phenomenon: a high energy, low voltage spark pulse current
momentarily generates spark plasma at high localized temperatures as shown in
Fig. 4, from several to 10,000 °C between the powder particles which causes
vaporization and the melting of the surfaces of the powder particles during the SPS
process, and constricted shapes or “necks” are formed around the contact area
between the powder particles. These necks gradually develop and plastic trans-
formation progresses during sintering, resulting in the sintered target of near 100%
density. Since only the surface temperature of the particles rises rapidly by
self-heating, the sintering temperatures are 200 –500 °C lower than that of the
conventional atmospheric pressure sintering, and the particle growth of the starting
powder materials is ef ﬁciently controlled. So SPS is the preferred method to
manufacture the target with high density and ﬁne grain size even nanometer scale
[16, 17]. For SPS, vaporization, melting and sintering are completed in short
periods of approximately 5 –20 min, including temperature rise and holding time,
which is much shorter than atmospheric pressure sintering, HP, or HIP. Currently
the key manufacture technology of SPS equipment is only mastered by very few
manufacturers, such as SPS Syntex Inc or NJS Co., Ltd SPS Center of Japan,
KCE-FCT of Germany, Dr Fritsch of Germany. The SPS equipment for the target
with less than diameter 200 mm is universal and popularly applied in enterprises of
USA, Europe, and Japan, but the equipment for the target with a large dimension,
such as larger than diameter 350 mm, is just in R&D stage. In China the total SPS is
less than 20 sets, which are mostly applied for scienti ﬁc research in the universities
and institutes. The main reason may be that the cost of SPS is very high, even
Sintering Fabrication and Characterizations of Powder … 1015

higher than HIP. However there is no question that SPS is very competitive due to
high efﬁciency in the future

guarantee the ﬁlm properties and reliability. It is desirable to reduce the following
impurities as much as possible: alkali metal elements such as Li, Na and K;
radioactive elements such as U and Th; and transition metal elements such as Fe,

Ni, Co, Cr and Cu; and gas impurities such as C, N, O and S [ 18]. The reason why
the mentioned metal impurities are harmful is that alkali metals move easily in the
gate insulator and cause the device to deteriorate, radioactive elements cause a soft
error of elements due to the a rays emitted from such elements, and transition metal
elements contained as impurities cause trouble at the interface bonding, and gas
impurities especially C and O effect the sintering character of the powder and lead
to the generation of particles during sputtering deposition. The analytical techniques
of the metal impurities in the IC target with less than 4N commonly include
Inductively Couples Plasma Spectroscopy (ICP-OES/MS), and 4N or higher purity
analytical techniques mainly include the Glow Discharge Mass Spectrometry
(GDMS), whose detection limits can reach ppm (one part per million), even ppb
(one part per billion). And the gas impurities are commonly evaluated based on
combustion and infrared technology. The purity grade standards mainly include
ASTM F2113-01and YS/T 935-2013 of Standard guide for analysis and reporting
the impurity content and grade of high purity metallic sputtering targets for elec-
tronic thin ﬁlm applications, as shown in Table 2.
Density The density is one of the most important performance indexes for PM
targets. The density of targets used in IC is usually required higher than 95% of the
theoretical density. Because low density means that there are many void in the
target. And a previous study indicated that the voids in the target may act as a
particle source during sputtering, thus lowering production yield [ 19]. Since the
particle defect control is critical in semiconductor devices. Besides, the gas inclu-
sions especially O
2 in the voids can low the ﬁlm purity during sputtering deposition.
It is also indicated that the erosion rate of the target and the ﬁlm deposition rate are
functions of the target density [ 5]. It was found that the higher of the target density,
the higher of the erosion rate and ﬁlm deposition. The analytical method of target
density is Archimedes ’s principle, and the standards include GB/T5163, ISO 3369,
and etc.
Grain Size and Grain Orientation Grain size and grain orientation may affect the
ﬁlm uniformity, so they are also the major performance factors of the PM target. It
is expected that the grains are ﬁne, uniform and equal-axed, and there are no or
weak textures in the target. The grain size of the target mainly depends on powder
and parameters of sintering temperature, press, holding time and so on. The grain

should consider the different angles, different radius, and different thickness in the

Sintering of Nano Molybdenum Powder
Bohua Duan, Zhao Zhang and Dezhi Wang
Abstract Molybdenum is a rare refractory metal with low thermal expansion
coefﬁcient, good thermal and electrical conductivity, high modulus of elasticity.
However, the plasticity and processing properties of molybdenum restrict its
application in the ﬁeld of high technology. In the present paper the sintering process
mainly by conventional sintering based on the nano molybdenum powders was
studied, the effects of powder size, sintering temperature and soaking time on the
density, microstructure, mechanical and physical properties of molybdenum prod-
ucts analysed. The experimental results show that nano Mo powder compact had a
lower temperature to densi ﬁcation compared with micron-powder compact. It is
suggested that 1550 °C is the most appropriate temperature to obtain the best
mechanical and physical properties.

/C1Sintering /C1Nanopowder
Introduction
Molybdenum (Mo) is a refractory metal that keeps its body-centred cubic
(bcc) crystal structure from room temperature of 25 °C all the way to its high
melting temperature of 2,610 °C [ 1]. It has characteristics of high melting point,
high thermal conductivity, high mechanical strength, and high modulus of elasticity
[1, 3]. Some of the important uses are electrodes for electrically heated glass

furnaces and forehearths, nuclear energy applications, missile and aircraft parts,

as an alloying agent in steel [ 2].
Nano powder material refers to the particle size in the range of 1 –100 nm
ultraﬁne particles. Compare with micron-powder, nano powder has the small size
effects, surface effects, quantum size effects and quantum tunneling effects, and they
have different properties in sound, light, electricity, magnetism, heat and mechanics,
which are different from those of large particle powders. The application of nano
powder to powder metallurgy process can reduce sintering temperature and improve
the properties of powder metallurgy products. Recently, a little research has been
carried out about sintering used by nano molybdenum powders. In this work, the
sintering rule of nano molybdenum powder was studied mainly by conventional
sintering.
Experiment Procedure
Molybdenum of average crystallite size of 40 nm powders was supplied by Yaotian
New Material Technology, Shanghai, CHN. Nano powders mixed with 1% poly-
vinyl alcohol (PVA) were pressed in a die of 1.5 cm inner diameter with the
pressing pressure of 200 MPa to make the green compacts of approximately 0.7 –
0.8 cm in height and the green density was around 60 –65% theoretically. Then, the
green compacts were sintered by conventional sintering in a tubular resistance
furnace (model: SK2-6-10, supplier: Kexin furnace, Changsha, China). The
experiment set the temperature of 1500, 1550, 1600 °C and soaking time of 30, 60,
90, 120 min. The sintering atmosphere was 90% Ar + 10% H2.
The density of the sintered samples was measured by Archimedes drainage.
Then the microstructure and morphology of the sintered samples were analyzed by
environmental scanning electron microscopy (model: Quanta FEI 200, supplier:
FEI Electron Optics B.V, Netherlands). To measure the Vickers hardness of the
sintered samples digital microhardness tester (model: HVS-1000 digital, supplier:
Huxing Optical Instrument Factory, Shanghai, China) was used. Finally, we tested
the electrical conductivity of the sintered samples by digital metal conductivity
measuring instrument (mdel: D60K, supplier: Gaozhi Precision instrument,
Shanghai, China).
Results and Discussion
Effect of Sintering Temperature Figure 1 compares the densities of the sintered
samples at different sintering temperatures after the same soaking time. It ’s easy to
observe that as the heating temperature rising up, the density increases continu-
ously, and the density of sintered samples made by nano powder are signi ﬁcantly

## Page 993

The sintered density of compacts made by nano powder increases from 80 to 94%
while there is not so much change in sintered density of compacts made by micron
powder under the same conditions. The general consensus in the literature has
converged to the fact that for nano particle sizes the onset of densi ﬁcation occurs at
lower temperatures of 0.2 –0.4T
m (Tm— melting temperature in K) compared to 0.5 –
0.8Tm for micron-sized powders. That ’s because the grain boundary of
nano-structured powder compact has the phenomenon of sliding and rotation and
viscous ﬂowing so that signi ﬁcantly contribute to densi ﬁcation enhancement [ 4–7].
As can be seen from Fig. 3, the hardness and electrical conductivity of samples
increase ﬁrst and then decrease, and when the temperature is at 1550 °C, the sample
has the maximum performance in both two indices. Hardness and electrical con-
ductivity mainly depend on the porosity and microstructure defects, and they also
depend on the grain size. The smaller grain size is, the more grain boundaries are,
so that the more dislocations are trapped, leading a better hardness and electrical
conductivity. In addition, when the temperature reaches a certain range, the change
of shrinkage, hardness and electrical conductivity of samples are not obvious, but
the grain size is increasing quickly. The coarsening of grain size leads to the
decrease of comprehensive properties.
Mondal et al. [ 3] also reported about 95% of density in case of conventional
sintered compacts. However, in their experiments the compacts made by
sub-micron powder were sintered at a very high temperature (2000 °C). It indicates
that the spherical nano powder can really reduce the sintering temperature. It also
can therefore be inferred that more sintering temperature points need to be selected
to study.

Effect of Soaking Time Figures 4 and 5 show the effect of samples in different
soaking time under conventional sintering. As the soaking time is increasing, the
density is also increasing, and the grain size increasing as well (Fig. 6).
This is because the grain is growing up with the extending of the soaking time,
which promotes the diffusion of vacancies. The density has been increasing out of
the rearrangement of particles and the transport of viscous and plastic ﬂows. But
with the increasing of soaking time, the grain growth rate will be much larger than
the nucleation rate, which will lead to abnormal grain growth after a certain period
of time.

In conclusion, extension of soaking time can make the material have a higher

## Page 997

Conclusion
Spherical nano molybdenum powder compacts are successfully consolidated and
densiﬁed through conventional sintering. It is interesting to note that the general
consensus in the literature has converged to the fact that for nano particle sizes the
onset of densi ﬁcation occurs at lower temperatures. This is attributed to the fact that
the compact ’s grain boundary sliding and rotation, and viscous ﬂow of
nano-structured powders signi ﬁcantly contribute to densi ﬁcation enhancement [ 4–
7], which leads a much lower sintering temperature and shorter soaking time than
micron powders. Therefore, nano powders are easier to be densi ﬁed than micron
powders under the same sintering conditions. Moreover, due to the low sintering
temperature, nano powder has less energy consuming compared with the equivalent
condition of material being consolidated by micron powder. Another common
observation is that the microwave sintering takes only half of the time to achieve the
same result as the conventional sintering does, and it still has very large develop-
ment space.

Migration of Liquid Phase
in Dual-Layer WC-9Ni Cemented
Carbides
Kaihua Shi, Xiuqi Zan and Liao Jun
Abstract The liquid phase migration (LPM) in the sintering process of WC-9Ni
dual-layer cemented carbides and its mechanism were investigated and discussed
using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) with energy dispersive spectroscopy
(EDS) system. Moreover, the effect of sintering temperature and WC grain size on
micro-structure changes of the samples was also studied. The results indicated that
the LPM of dual-layer cemented carbide at different stages in the sintering process
was mainly dominated by capillary force, the decrease of inter-facial energy in ﬁne
WC layer (FWC layer) and Ni content concentration gradient in the coarse WC
layer (CWC layer). During the sintering process, liquid phase ﬁrst migrated from
FWC layer to CWC layer due to the effect of capillary force. With the temperature
increase, the liquid phase in turn ﬂowed from CWC layer to FWC layer resulted
from the decrease of inter-facial energy of FWC layer. A high temperature sintering
(1450 °C) might lead to the formation of an abnormal WC grain growth layer
(AWC layer) with relative high Ni content and many pool defects in the CWC layer
next to the interface. With the increase of WC particle size in the CWC layer, the
quantity of the pool defects in the CWC layer near the interface increased, so did
the size.

Introduction
Cemented carbide wear parts, such as oil nozzles and sealing rings, are typically
used in petroleum exploitation and water treatment ﬁelds. The service environment
of these ﬁelds is terrible, the parts have to face to high stresses and temperatures,
normally in corrosive conditions. Therefore, apart from the properties of hardness
and strength, the alloys used in these environments should show a good combi-
nation of oxidation and corrosion resistance [ 1]. Among all the new binding metals
investigated for cemented carbides, Ni is considered to be one of the most potential
material mainly due to its excellent plasticity and corrosion resistance [ 2]. WC-Ni
cemented carbides have better oxidation and corrosion resistance than that of tra-
ditional WC-Co cemented carbides [ 3, 4]. Studies indicate that WC-Ni –Cr
cemented carbide is signi ﬁcantly superior to that of the traditional WC-Co grades
on corrosion resistance in the immersion corrosion and electrochemical tests in
acidic conditions (HNO
3,H 2SO4, HCl) [ 5].
Nevertheless, it is known that the mechanical properties such as hardness and
strength of WC-Ni cemented carbide are relatively inferior to those of WC-Co
alloys [ 6, 7]. In consequence, most of the studies were focused on the properties
improvement of WC-Ni based cemented carbides [ 8–10]. On the contrary, few
attentions have been paid on the micro-structure change, such as migration of liquid
phase, during the liquid phase sintering process, even if we know that sintering is a
very important process for cemented carbides producing [ 11].
In this study, dual-layer WC-Ni cemented carbides were taken as the object of
study. The micro-structure and composition at different positions in the WC-Ni
cemented carbide bodies after sintering at different temperature are presented.
The LPM at the interfaces and the migration mechanism were investigated and
discussed in this paper.
Experimental
WC with different initial grain size and nickel powders were weighted to form
initial powder mixture of investigated samples. All these chemicals are of analytical
reagent grade and were used as received without further puri ﬁcation. The SEM
micro-graphs of WC with different initial grain sizes are shown in Fig. 1a–f and the
chemical compositions of WC-9Ni powder mixture are given in Table 1. It should
be noticed that there are 0.5 wt% Cr as the grain growth inhibitor in the ﬁnest WC
powders (WC-1 in Table 1). The powders were mixed by ball milling, which was
described in detail elsewhere [ 12]. After ball milling, the slurry was dried in a 60 °C
oven for 60 min to obtain the powders for pressing.
The dual-layer cemented carbides were made up with two-steps pressing: ﬁrst
ﬁne WC-9Ni powder was compacted in a carbide die at 40 MPa to form the ﬁne
WC layer (FWC), and then coarse WC-9Ni powder was put into the mold to form

All the samples were placed on a graphite tray and then sintered in an HIP-Sinter

Sintering at 1400 °C Figure 3a–e show the SEM photos of interfaces of the

layer because of capillary forces [ 13]. This is then con ﬁrmed by EDS. Figure 4 is

the increase of the WC particle size in the CWC layer, the effect of the liquid phase
migration on the formation of pools defects became more obvious, which lead to a
bigger size of the pools. In addition, it can be seen in Fig. 4 that the content of Ni in
CWC layer near the interface is approximately 1 –2 wt% less than that in the FWC
layer. In the latter, it is identical with the nominal composition (9 wt%) far away
from the interface.
Sintering at 1450 °C When the samples were sintered at 1450 °C, which means
that the liquid phase sintering time of CWC layer is enough, the dual-layer WC-9Ni
cemented carbides showed an obviously different liquid phase migration and

## Page 1004

micro-structure change with the sample sintered at 1400 °C. Figure 5a–e show the
SEM photos of the diffusion interface of dual-layer samples after sintered at 1450 °
C for 90 min.
In Fig. 5, after sintered at high temperature, 5 groups of dual-layer samples
exhibited a similar micro-structure change, namely an AWC layer formed in the
CWC layer next to the diffusion interface. In this layer, a large number of pools
were found. The EDS results (see Fig. 6) show that the liquid phase (mainly Ni)
content in different positions in the samples have signi ﬁcant difference.
In Fig. 6, it can be seen that from CWC layer to AWC layer the Ni content
increases gradually and reached 12.5 wt%. In the FWC layer, the Ni content is
relatively uniform and close to the nominal Ni content (9 wt%).
Generally, it was believed that the mechanism of the LPM from CWC layer to
FWC layer may be the capillary force on the diffusion interface [ 13]. According to
this theory, due to the effect of capillary force in sintering process, Ni will con-
tinuously transfer from the side with relatively large mean free path to the other side
with lower mean free path, until the difference of the mean free path disappears.
However, it is known that only in the three-phase (solid phase, liquid phase and gas
phase) interface can the capillary force play a role [ 14]. Which means that, in the
liquid phase sintering stage of WC-Ni cemented carbide, capillary force will not act
because there are exist only solid and liquid phases without gas phase. Therefore,
the point of view which the capillary force is the main mechanism of the liquid
phase migration from CWC layer to FWC layer in the samples has certain
limitations.

## Page 1006

Accordingly, a new opinion was proposed: the liquid phase transfer driving
force comes from the change of the inter-facial energy, because the inter-facial
energy has a tendency to reduce spontaneously [ 15]. As shown in Fig. 7a, before
the liquid phase migration, the FWC layer has a larger solid-solid contact area and
low solid-liquid contact area, which caused a higher total inter-facial energy.
Therefore, in the FWC layer, the inward migration pressure of liquid phase is higher
than that of the outward, which drives the liquid phase of the CWC layer into the
FWC layer. Along with the migration the volume fraction of liquid phase of the
FWC layer increases, thus promoting the rotation and rearrangement of WC grain,
leading to the decrease of solid-solid contact area and increase of solid-liquid
contact area as shown in Fig. 7b. Therefore, the total inter-facial energy and inward
migration pressure of liquid phase of FWC layer decrease. The liquid phase
migration will not stop until the total inter-facial energy in the FWC layer equal that
of the CWC layer and the inward and outward liquid phase migration pressure is
equal to zero.
In order to ﬁnd out whether this assumption is applicable for the dual-layer
WC-Ni system, one sample (sample 5) was chosen and sintered at 1450 °C for a
longer holding time (3 h). After sintering, the micro-structure near the interface was
observed and shown in Fig. 8. In the picture, a new layer with thicker binder phase
after liquid phase migration was formed in the FWC layer. This maybe because the
liquid phase migrated to FWC layer and increased the inter-facial energy of the
FWC layer near interface.
According to the above discussion of the theory of liquid phase migration, we
speculate that in the liquid phase sintering stage, the liquid phase migration process
is mainly as follows. First, when the temperature reached the eutectic point of the
FWC layer, the liquid phase migrated from FWC layer to CWC layer due to the
capillary force. Afterwards, with the temperature continued to rise, the liquid phase
in turn ﬂown from CWC layer near the interface to FWC layer. Consequently, the
liquid phase in the CWC layer distal migrated to the interface in order to replenish
Fig. 7 A schematic drawing explaining the driving force for the liquid phase migration
phenomenon
1038 K. Shi et al.

## Page 1007

the loss of Ni. Finally, after a relatively long time migration, Ni mainly concen-
trated in the CWC layer near the interface because the FWC layer densifying
hindered further ﬂow of the liquid phase. In this area, the existence of a large
amount of liquid phase caused the abnormal WC grain growth by dissolution and
precipitation mechanism, thus leading to the formation of the AWC layer with high
Ni content and a mass of pool defects. And, of course, the sintering process of
dual-layer cemented carbide itself is very complicated. Hence, further in-depth
researches on the liquid phase migration and micro-structure change are very
necessary.
Conclusions
The WC-9Ni mixtures with varieties of initial WC grain sizes have been prepared to
form the dual-layer cemented carbides. The liquid phase migration in the sintering
process and its mechanism have been investigated and discussed, and moreover, the
micro-structure changes of the samples caused by the liquid phase migration also
observed. The major conclusions are summarized as follows.
The liquid phase migration mechanisms of dual-layer cemented carbides in the
sintering process are mainly the capillary force when three phase coexistence,
decrease of inter-facial energy in FWC layer and Ni content concentration gradient
in CWC layer. In the sintering process, liquid phase ﬁrst appears in FWC layer due
to the relatively low eutectic point and migrates to CWC layer due to the effect of
capillary force. With the temperature continue to rise and reach the eutectic point of
CWC layer, the liquid phase in turn ﬂow from CWC layer near the interface to
FWC layer result from the domination of inter-facial energy balance. When the
Fig. 8 SEM photo of the diffusion interface of dual-layer samples after sintering at 1450 °C for 3 h
Migration of Liquid Phase in Dual-Layer WC-9Ni Cemented Carbides 1039

## Page 1008

sintering temperature is high enough, the Ni content concentration gradient in the
CWC layer actuates the liquid phase migration from the position away from
interface to the area near the interface.
Sintering temperature and WC grain size have signi ﬁcant effect on the
micro-structure of WC-Ni cemented carbide. When the sintering temperature is low
(1400 °C), pool defects result from liquid phase migration were found in the CWC
layer near the interface. When sintering at a high temperature (1450 °C), in CWC
layer at the side of the interface, a AWC layer with relative high Ni content and
many pool defects has been found. Under different sintering temperature, with the
increase of WC particle size in CWC layer, the quantity and size of the pools
increase.

Jingbo Fu, Weicheng Cao, Geng An, Qinli Yang, Fei Zhuang,
Xiao Zhang, Pengfa Feng and Chunyang Bo
Abstract TZM alloys used as isothermal forging die at high temperature were
prepared by a new powder doping process combined with the rational design of
sintering technique and hot working technology. In this paper, tensile properties of
TZM alloys at room temperature and properties such as tensile properties, fracture
toughness and stress rupture at elevated temperatures were investigated. The results
show that the mechanical properties at room temperature were excellent in accord
with the ASTM B386-03 (2011) standard. At the temperature of 1100 °C, the
tensile and yield strength were 552 and 514 Mpa respectively, and the endurance
life is 250 h under the load stress of 160 Mpa, the TZM alloys can be used as
isothermal forging die material at temperature of 1100 °C or above.

With the development of China ’s defense industry, application of aviation materials
hard to machine are used wider and wider. At the same time, deformation process of
those materials has become a crucial issue. Now days, the deformation method of
the aviation materials hard to machine is isothermal Forging at elevated temperatures

[1–3]. So, to ﬁnd a mould material used as isothermal forging die becomes the most
important thing. Mo base alloys are featured with good thermal conductivity, low
expansion coef ﬁcient and slow softening at high temperatures. The small thermal
stress under rapid heating and cooling, and the little expansion coefﬁcient result in no
size changing of the mould during work [ 4, 5]. At the same time, Mo alloys have
properties such as high strength at room or elevated temperatures, good fracture
toughness and stress rupture properties. All these advantages become the main rea-
sons for them to be thermal mould materials [ 6]. Applications of Mo alloys in the
aspect of tool and mould are as piercing plug for stainless steel tube, die casting
mould for black metals and copper alloys, extrusion mould and isothermal forging
die, etc. [ 7].
According to the reference [ 6], Mo alloys used as tool and mould are TZM and
TZC alloys. Compared with TZM alloy, TZC alloy has superior thermal strength
and recrystallization temperature, but it is not only hard to machine, but also has
poor fracture toughness properties, so it ’s application is limited. While TZM alloy
has excellent comprehensive properties and is widely used. Now, TZM alloy is the
uniqueness used as the tool and mould material for the isothermal forging powder
of plate parts of super alloy, but for some reason the research on this aspect was not
carried out in China.
The main chemical compositions of TZM alloy are as follows: 0.4 –0.55 wt% Ti,
0.06–0.10 wt% Zr, 0.01 –0.04 wt% C [ 8]. During the preparation of TZM alloy, to
control the oxygen content is the critical point. In this research, conventional
hydrogenides [ 9–11] such as TiH
2 and ZrH 2 used as additives were replaced by
carbides to make TZM alloy powders, combining with vacuum and hydrogen
multi-steps sintering, thus the TZM alloy with low oxygen content was prepared.
The properties of TZM alloy at room and elevated temperatures were mainly
studied.
Experimental Procedures
In this work, the pure Mo powders with a particle size of 3 lm were used as the raw
material, TiC and ZrC powders of −300 mesh were used as additives. TiC, ZrC and
the Mo powders were mixed in a three dimensional mixer for 4 h to make the TZM
alloy powders. The morphologies of those powers are as Fig. 1. The TZM powders
were consolidated at 180 MPa by cold isostatic pressing, followed by two steps
sintering of vaccum or H
2 atmosphere. And the size of the sintered billet was about
32 mm /C2180 mm /C2135 mm, with the density of 9.76 g/cm 3. The chemical
composition of the billet is as Table 1. The billet was rolled at 1300 °C. The
thickness of products were 5, 3 and 2 mm respectively. The stress relieving tem-
perature was at 1100 °C.
The mechanical properties at room temperature was carried on the universal
testing machine based on the testing standard of ASTM-E8-2015a, tensile testing at
high temperatures of 1100, 1200 and 1600 °C were conducted on ultra high

YKM-2200 machine at 1100 °C, the high temperature endurance was conducted on
the ultra high temperature creep test machine based on the standard of GB/T
2039-2012, under the load of 130, 160 and 240 Mpa respectively. All the fracture
morphologies were observed by HITACHIS-3400 scanning electron microscope.

Summary
The TZM alloy prepared by the new process obtained good properties. Both the
mechanical property of the TZM alloy at room temperature and chemical content of
oxygen (O) are in accord with the ASTM B 386-2003(2011) standard. Compared
with the other domestic materials used for isothermal forging die at 1100 °C, the
TZM alloy has obvious advantages, such as higher tensile properties and strength
rupture properties at 1100 °C. So the TZM alloy can be used as isothermal forging
die material at the temperature of 1100 °C or above.

Abstract The evolution of density of tungsten sheets with different dopant content
is studied. The microstructure evolution and annealing behavior of three kinds of
tungsten sheets with deformation of 63, 83, 92%, are studied. The results show that
when rolling deformation reaches to 92%, the density of lanthanum-doped tungsten
sheets increases from 18.4 to 18.9 g/cm
3, and the density of Potassium-doped
tungsten sheets increases from 17.6 to 19.15 g/cm 3. The deformation of lanthanum
oxide particles increases with the increment of deformation, and the tungsten sheets
exhibit a typical rolling state. The microstructure of doped tungsten sheets at high
temperature is more stable than that of the pure tungsten ones.

Introduction
Tungsten is a refractory metal. The high melting point, high temperature strength,
low vapor pressure, low coef ﬁcient of thermal expansion, as well as good thermal
and electrical conductivity are the basis for application in furnace and electronics
ﬁelds. In recent years, with the development of LED industry, there is a stronger
demand and higher performance for tungsten products [ 1–3]. For example, Veeco ’s
MOCVD equipment requires that tungsten heaters are able to withstand a long
service lives at higher temperatures up to 1800 °C, and guarantee the product ’s
dimensional stability. So it requires a higher temperature creep resistance of
tungsten heater. However, for industrial production, pure tungsten heater is prone to
deformation, resulting in heating power ﬂuctuations, affecting the quality of LED
chip stability, therefore, it is of great signi ﬁcance to improve the high temperature

The purpose of this work is to study the density evolution and microstructure
evolution of tungsten sheets with different dopant content in sheet rolling process.
Providing technical support for the optimization of hot-rolling process, and
obtaining doped tungsten sheets and products which meet the requirements of
customers.
Experiment
Sheets Rolling The pure tungsten powder (PW), lanthanated tungsten powder
(LaW) and potassium-doped tungsten (ASKW) powder with different grain size as
raw materials, respectively, was shaped by cold isostatic pressing(CIP). The
employed pressure for pressing was 200 Mpa. The sintering process was carried out
in furnace with Intermediate Frequency heating. The protection atmosphere for
sintering was hydrogen. The maximum temperature was 2300 °C and holding time
was 6 h. The sintered plate was ﬁnished with a thickness of 30 mm. Then the
sintered plate was hot-rolled to a thickness of 2.5 mm. The chemical composition of
various powders is shown in Table 1.
During hot-rolling process, samples were taken from the as-rolled sheet with dif-
ferent thickness. The hot-rolling temperature reaches to 1300 –1650 °C, holding
time is 30 –60 min.
Annealing Recrystallization annealing for 10 h at 1600 °C in hydrogen atmo-
sphere was carried out for three kinds of sheets with a thickness of 2.5 mm.
Characterization The density of the samples was determined by Archimedes
drainage method. The transverse interface of different thickness tungsten plates was
observed by metallographic microscope, and the Vickers hardness of the samples
was measured. The fracture morphology was analyzed by SEM (S3400N model,
Hitachi, Japan).

grain’s growth, and in the hot rolling process, apparent dynamic recrystallization

Conclusion
(1) As the amount of rolling deformation increases, the density of the tungsten plate
increases. When the amount of rolling deformation is 92%, the relative density of
pure tungsten, potassium-doped tungsten and lanthanum-doped tungsten plate is
higher than 99.2%, meeting the density requirements on the tungsten sheet.
(2) With the increase of rolling deformation, the thickness of the plate decreases,
the hole disappears, the aspect ratio of the tungsten grains increases, and the
typical rolling occurs. When the deformation is more than 60%, the tungsten
particles are signi ﬁcantly stretched, showing a layered microstructure.
(3) In terms of microstructure control of the doped sheet, the processing conditions
of the initial rolling stage have a greater effect on the control of the ﬁnal sheet.
(4) The microstructure of Potassium doped and lanthanum-doped tungsten sheet is
more stable than pure tungsten plate at high temperature. Potassium doped and
lanthanum-doped tungsten plate exhibit higher high temperature creep resistance.

## Page 1025

Effect of Nd-Doping
on the Microstructure and Magnetic
Properties of Nd X(Fe47.5Pd52.5)100-X
Films
Jianjun Huo, Gang Cheng, Yusong Du, Kuang Pan and Lin Li
Abstract In order to investigate the effect of rare earth Nd doping on FePd alloy
thin ﬁlms, the samples of Nd x(Fe47.5Pd52.5)100-x (x = 0, 2, 2.7, 3.4, 4) ﬁlms were
prepared by a DC magnetic sputtering method. The microstructure and magnetic
properties were characterized by XRD, EDS, PPMS et al. The XRD data indicated
that the addition of rare earth element Nd could signi ﬁcantly shorten the annealing
time and the annealing temperature from the disordered FCC phase to the ordered
FCT phase and increase the driving force of the phase transition. In addition, the
appropriate addition of Nd element also has the role of grain re ﬁnement. The grain
size could reach 29 –14 nm and the appropriate grain size was conducive to the
exchange coupling between the grains. The hysteresis loop of the ﬁlms showed that
the coercivity (Hc) and remanence ratio (Mr/Ms) ﬁrst increased with the increase of
Nd content sharply and then decreased. When the content of rare earth x = 2.7, the
maximum coercivity was 3.05 kOe. The changes of coercivity and remanence ratio
with the increase of annealing temperature also ﬁrst increased and then decreased,
and reached the maximum at 550 °C.
Keywords FePd ﬁlms
/C1 Nd doping /C1 Heat treatment /C1 Magnetization
Introduction
With the rapid development of information technology, the demand for large
capacity information storage devices is increasing rapidly. It has been paid attention
to by the researchers in the past to search for high density magnetic recording

devices. 1L 0 ordered phase FePd alloy (K U =1 0 7erg/cm3) with high magne-
tocrystalline anisotropy and high coercivity. Theoretically, The maximum magnetic
energy product is 48.0 MGOe [ 1]. These unique and excellent comprehensive
properties are considered to be one of the best materials for ultrahigh density
magnetic recording media and micro-electromechanical systems [ 2].
In recent years, a lot of research work mainly focused on the origin of the ordered
L1
0 phase FePd alloy with high magnetocrystalline anisotropy [ 3–6] and to explore a
variety of physical and chemical methods for the preparation of various alloy ﬁlms,
such as FePd alloy ﬁlm [7–9], FePd/Fe multilayer ﬁlm, [10] nanowire [11] and nano
particles [12]. In order to improve the magnetic properties of the alloy ( ﬁlm), doping
or alloying is the main method to improve the properties of materials [ 13–15]. The
results show that if the FePd alloy nanocrystalline particles added in the C element, it
will signi ﬁcantly hinder the diffusion of Fe and Pd atoms and it can inhibit the
conversion of FePd nanoparticles from disordered FCC phase to ordered FCT phase
[16], the comprehensive performance of the alloy can be improved.
At present, the effects of rare earth elements on the magnetic properties of FePd
alloy thin ﬁlms and their role in the microstructure evolution and order-disorder
phase transition have not been systematically studied. In this paper, a series of Nd –
Fe–Pd thin ﬁlms were prepared by DC magnetic sputtering. The effects of Nd
content and annealing temperature on the structure and magnetic properties of
Nd
x(Fe47.5Pd52.5)100-x thin ﬁlms were studied by changing the content of rare earth
Nd and annealing temperature.
Experiment
The thin ﬁlm samples of Nd x(Fe47.5Pd52.5)100-x (x = 2, 2.7, 3.4, 4) were prepared by
ultrahigh vacuum multi target magnetron sputtering. Rare earth Nd doped FePd
layer by alternating deposition method. Nd rare earth ﬁlms were uniformly placed
on the FePd composite target (the purities of the ingredients were better than
99.9 wt%) and the content of rare earth in FePd layer was controlled by changing
the number of rare earth ﬁlms. It could be considered that the addition of rare earth
will not change the proportion of the FePd layer and the total thickness because the
rare earth was very few in the sputtering. In the experiment, the purity of the rare
earth was not less than 99.5%. Before using, the Nd target was carefully cleaned
and placed on the sputtering target of excitation. Before the deposition of thin ﬁlms,
the “pre sputtering ” ready for 30 min to remove the oxide layer and the target
surface impurities. In this study, Nd
x(Fe47.5Pd52.5)100-x thin ﬁlms were prepared by
FJL560B4 ultra-high vacuum magnetron sputtering and the vacuum degree of the
sputtering system was better than 6.5 /C2 10
−5 Pa. The sputtering gas was argon and
the sputtering pressure was 2.0 Pa. The ﬁlms were sealed by argon ﬁlled under
vacuum condition (10 −1 Pa) and annealing in muf ﬂe furnace. Annealing tempera-
ture at 500, 550 and 600 °C, the holding time was 30 min. The deposition rates
measured by an AMBIOS XP-2 stylus pro ﬁlometer; the structure of annealed ﬁlms

Results and Discussion
Figure 1 shows X-ray diffraction patterns for Nd x(Fe47.5Pd52.5)100-x (x = 0, 2, 2.7,
3.4, 4) thin ﬁlm samples annealed at 550 °C for 30 min. As can be seen from the
graph, the undoped ﬁlm samples are basically composed of FCC phase at the same
annealing conditions. When the content of Nd is 2 at.%, the weak FCT phase
diffraction peak can be observed. With the further increase of Nd content, the
intensity of the diffraction peak of FCT phase increases gradually. When the Nd
content increases to 4 at.%, it is obvious to see the FCT phase diffraction peak,
which is an ordered FCT phase, which means that the addition of Nd element can
promote the phase transition of FCC — FCT. The result is that the phase transition
temperature of FePd alloy ﬁlms decreases with the increase of Nd content.
According to the diffraction data of alloy thin ﬁlms, the lattice parameters of the
FCC phase have been derived, and the results are shown in Table 1. Table 1 shows
that the lattice parameter a increases in a near-linear fashion with increasing of Nd
concentration. This indicates that the Nd atoms dissolved into the FCC phase,
forming a solid solution, which leads to a cell-volume expansion resulting from the
fact that the Nd atom radius is larger than those of both Fe and Pd atoms.
We calculated the c/a ratio and the order degree S

doping amount, the corresponding sample c/a ratio was decreased gradually; the
order degree increased to a certain extent. This indicates that the addition of rare
earth element Nd can enhance the driving force of phase transformation and

The factors that affect the coercivity are the magnetic anisotropy constant, the
exchange coupling coef ﬁcient between grains, the concentration of FCT phase and
the degree of order. According to the model of Kneller and Hawig [ 17], exchange
coupling effect of the hard magnetic phase (k) and soft magnetic phase (m) is
determined by the grain size. In the system of exchange coupled
nanocomposite-magnet, the critical size of the exchange-coupling can be calculated
according to the following formula:
b
cm ¼ p Am=2KkðÞ 1=2 ð1Þ
where A m is the exchange interaction energy of soft magnetic phase, K k is the
magnetic anisotropy constant of the hard magnetic phase. In order to obtain a strong
exchange coupling magnetic phase, the grain size of soft phase should be about
equal to b
cm. The result shows that, when the grain size is less than 20 nm and
uniform size, the exchange coupling effect between soft and hard magnetic phase
can not only enhance the remanence Br, but also can increase the coercivity (Hc), so
as to obtain high magnetic energy product. From the experimental data of XRD
ﬁlm, under the same heat treatment conditions, the more the concentration of rare
earth Nd, the intensities of the FCT phase characteristic peaks (110), (200) (002)
were stronger, and the splitting degrees of diffraction peak (200) and (002) were
greater. This shows that the larger the volume fraction of FCT phase in the ﬁlm, the
higher the degree of order, the greater the anisotropy constant. When x exceeds 2.7,
it is possible that the grain size is smaller than the optimum size of the exchange
coupling, and lead to the coupling between soft and hard magnetic phase is
weakened. Another possible reason is that the concentration of rare earth Nd
exceeds the solid solution range of the FePd alloy, which makes the rare earth
elements gather around the grain, which increases the distance between the grains
and weakens the exchange coupling effect, which leads to further decreasing in Hc.

Hc ¼ Kk =l0Msm ð2Þ
where Msm is the saturation magnetization of the soft magnetic phase and K k is the
anisotropy constant of the hard magnetic phase. The higher remanence ratio sug-
gests that exchange-coupling occurs between the soft magnetic phase and the hard
magnetic phase. When the annealing temperature is higher than 550 °C, the coer-
civity and remanence ratio are beginning to decline. The reason is that when the
annealing temperature increases, the grain size becomes larger, and the optimum
size of coupling is removed, which leads to the decrease of coupling effect. Another
possibility is because when the annealing temperature is too high, rare earth ele-
ments separate out from FePd alloys and enriched in grain boundaries, and the
distance between the grains become larger, which affects the exchange coupling
effect between grains, while the coercivity and remanence ratio also decreased. This
is why coercivity and remanence ratio decreases with increasing of annealing
temperature for FePd ﬁlms.
Conclusion
The addition of rare earth element Nd in FePd alloy ﬁlm can signi ﬁcantly shorten
the transition time from FCC phase to FCT phase and decrease the annealing
temperature, which indicates that adding moderate amount of rare earth Nd can
increase the driving force of phase transformation. When small amounts of Nd are
substituted for FePd, the Nd atoms dissolve into the FCC phase, forming a solid
solution. The addition of Nd leads to an increase in the degree of ordering S and a
decrease in the average grain size. The function relationship between the coercivity
of FePd thin ﬁlms and the rare earth Nd content increases sharply and then
decreases. For Nd
x(Fe47.5Pd52.5)100-x (x = 0, 2, 2.7, 3.4, 4) alloys ﬁlms, the maxi-
mum value of the coercivity and remanence ratio (Hc = 3.05 kOe, Mr/Ms = 0.646)
are obtained in x = 2.7. With the increase of annealing temperature, the change of
Nd2.7(Fe47.5Pd52.5)97.3 alloys ﬁlms also ﬁrst increases and then decreases, and the
maximum value of Hc = 3.05 kOe has obtained at 550 °C for 30 min. Therefore, a
small amount of rare earth doped (x < 2.7 at.%) and appropriate temperature
conditions can improve the magnetic properties of the ﬁlms.
